scope: Incremental source-visible payload of the seeded-history admitted reference-Richards temporal service only; excludes the principal Richards request/result/workspace that exists in both A and B arms.

persistent_optional_continuation_payload.notes: This is optional numerical continuation data, not solver scratch. Descriptor/allocator metadata is excluded from the byte formula.

lifetime_reasoning.peak_location: Inside evaluate_reference_richards_temporal_indicator after the operator/defect arrays are allocated and before subroutine return.
lifetime_reasoning.why_19_transient_vectors_overlap: The caller-owned previous_derivative and indicator_request copy remain live while the callee owns current_right_derivative plus sixteen local n-vectors.
lifetime_reasoning.history_replace_peak: After indicator return the sixteen local indicator work vectors have been automatically released. fkt_history_replace explicitly deallocates the old history before allocating the replacement, so source code does not require old and new persistent history payloads to coexist.
lifetime_reasoning.automatic_deallocation: Local allocatables in the indicator are procedure-local and are not persistent column state.

compute_and_allocation_operations_per_se.constitutive_evaluation: two full n-node evaluations into eight allocated result vectors
compute_and_allocation_operations_per_se.defect_linear_solve: one reference_tridag forward/backward O(n) sweep; no separately exposed factorization event
compute_and_allocation_operations_per_se.history_replace: explicit deallocate old payload, allocate n, O(n) copy

hard_nonclaims: 152*n is not a process RSS prediction.

160*n excludes allocatable descriptors, allocator bookkeeping, stack scalars, provider-internal temporaries, compiler-created expression temporaries and already-existing principal-solver request/result/workspace arrays.
No hidden compiler allocation is inferred from source inspection.
This artifact does not qualify a memory allocator, cache behavior, vectorization efficiency or worker-count scaling.
The current implementation uses per-call allocatables; PE06 does not change production source to pool or reuse them.

architecture_invariant_audit.4_compact_persistent_state: PASS_WITHIN_SCOPE: only the optional temporal-history layout carries one n-vector; inactive columns carry no history payload.
architecture_invariant_audit.5_scratch_per_worker: PASS_WITH_CAVEAT: indicator work arrays are transient and not committed column state. Current procedure-local allocation is compatible with non-persistent scratch semantics, although PE06 does not claim an optimized reusable worker scratch pool.
architecture_invariant_audit.16_multiswap_primary_use: OPEN_PERFORMANCE_IMPLICATION: 152*n source-visible transient bytes per active service call is O(n), but allocator churn and batch behavior require later runtime optimization/qualification if material at scale.
architecture_invariant_audit.27_optional_functionality_scales_with_us: PASS_WITHIN_SCOPE: persistent history exists only for the temporal-history continuation layout; indicator transient work occurs only when the service is invoked.
architecture_invariant_audit.30_architecture_change_audit: PASS: characterization only; no production source change.

optimization_observations_not_changes: The snapshot plus indicator-request copy creates two simultaneously live copies of the previous derivative before the indicator uses it.
The indicator currently allocates sixteen local work vectors on every admitted call in addition to current_right_derivative.
These are candidates for future worker-scratch reuse or interface-copy reduction, but no such optimization is admitted by F-PE06.
